headline: Araghchi blames US for Hormuz insecurity, calls for regional security arrangement without foreign forces
dek: Iranian FM Abbas Araghchi, at joint press conference with Russian FM Lavrov Monday, blamed the United States for insecurity and tensions in the Strait of Hormuz, said regional issues should be resolved through diplomacy, and called for regional countries to work toward a joint security arrangement…
fault_line: Regional security run by the region (no US bases) — vs — the strait only stays open BECAUSE of US power. Who do you trust to keep Hormuz open: Tehran+Moscow or Washington?

sections.what_happened: Iranian FM Abbas Araghchi, at joint press conference with Russian FM Lavrov Monday, blamed the United States for insecurity and tensions in the Strait of Hormuz, said regional issues should be resolved through diplomacy, and called for regional countries to work toward a joint security arrangement 'without the presence of foreign forces'.
sections.what_verified: Reuters wire reporting direct quotes from a public joint presser with Lavrov (presser itself confirmed by prior record 1600-06); consistent with Tehran's seven-day Hormuz proposal line (record 1600-05) and Moscow's standing anti-US-presence posture.
sections.what_disputed: US/CENTCOM position (public, via prior records): the strait's insecurity is Iran's mine-laying and the 14-point MoU violations; Washington insists nuclear concessions lead talks; Gulf states that want US presence reject the 'foreign forces' framing.
sections.why_matters: Tehran's gambit, in Tehran's own words: blame Washington for Hormuz insecurity while offering the strait back under a regional arrangement that excludes the US — published as Russia co-signs at the podium. Pair with the Axios limited-strike report and the Kharg plan: Tehran negotiates with one hand, girds with the other.
sections.context: Background: Araghchi blames US for Hormuz insecurity, calls for regional security arrangement without foreign forces — UPDATE (extends 1600-05, 1600-06)

totw_analysis: Our read: Tehran's gambit, in Tehran's own words: blame Washington for Hormuz insecurity while offering the strait back under a regional arrangement that excludes the US — published as Russia co-signs at the podium. Pair with the Axios limited-strike report and the Kharg plan: Tehran negotiates with one hand, girds with the other. The fault line our audience is arguing over: Regional security run by the region (no US bases) — vs — the strait only stays open BECAUSE of US power. Who do you trust to keep Hormuz open: Tehran+Moscow or Washington?
